symptom: The picker opens but has no styles

fix.text: Import `timepicker-ui/main.css` once, for example in your app's entry file. It contains the core styles and the default `basic` theme.
For another theme, also import `timepicker-ui/theme-<name>.css` and set `ui.theme` to the same name.

why: The package ships its CSS as separate files, so you load only the themes you use. `timepicker-ui/index.css` contains the core styles and all 12 themes in one file.

symptom: Nothing happens when the input is clicked

fix.text: Call `create()` after `new TimepickerUI(...)`. The handlers that open the picker on click and on Enter are added by `create()`, not by the constructor.
If the console shows `Input element not found`, the selector matched nothing when the code ran, or the element has no `<input>` inside it. Run the code after the element is in the page.

symptom: A range, timezone or wheel option is ignored, or an error event fires

fix.text: Import the plugin from `timepicker-ui/plugins/<name>` and pass it to `PluginRegistry.register()` once, before the first `new TimepickerUI(...)`.
A missing plugin is reported only through the `error` event, when the picker opens. Listen to it to see the message.

why: Each picker sets up its plugins in its constructor, so a plugin registered after `new TimepickerUI(...)` does not work in that picker. Without its plugin, the picker leaves out the range and timezone controls and shows the clock instead of the wheel. With `range.enabled` set, OK then does not close the picker.

fix.text: Pass your class name in `ui.cssClass` instead. The picker adds the class to `.tp-ui-wrapper` when it opens.
Set the `--tp-*` variables under `.tp-ui-wrapper.my-theme`. [CSS Variables](https://timepicker-ui.vercel.app/docs/api/css-variables) lists them.

why: `ui.theme` selects one of the 12 built-in themes. The picker writes the name to the `data-theme` attribute of the modal and does not add it as a class, so a rule such as `.my-theme` never matches.

symptom: TypeScript rejects a custom ui.theme name

fix.text: Leave `ui.theme` unset or use a built-in name, and pass your own class in `ui.cssClass`. [The `ui.theme` entry above](https://timepicker-ui.vercel.app/docs/guides/troubleshooting#uitheme-my-theme-has-no-effect) shows the CSS.

why: `ui.theme` is typed as a union of the 12 built-in theme names.

symptom: The modal shows behind a header or inside a clipped container

fix.text: If you set `ui.appendTo`, point it at an element outside the clipped container, or remove the option so the modal goes to `<body>`.
The modal has `z-index: 5000`. If your header has a higher `z-index`, lower the header's value, or raise the modal's in CSS that loads after `timepicker-ui/main.css`.

why: The modal is `position: fixed`. Inside an ancestor with `transform` or `filter`, a fixed element is placed relative to that ancestor instead of the viewport, and its `z-index` only counts inside it. `--tp-z-modal` is defined in `:root`, but no rule reads it, so changing it does nothing.

symptom: My CSS does not override the built-in styles

fix.text: Give the picker a class with `ui.cssClass`, for example `'my-picker'`.
Start each selector with `.tp-ui-wrapper.my-picker`. Built-in state rules such as `.tp-ui-hour.active` and `.tp-ui-hour.mobile.active` use two or three classes, and the prefix adds two more.
See [Specificity](https://timepicker-ui.vercel.app/docs/api/css-classes#specificity) on the CSS Classes page.

why: A rule loses when it has fewer classes than the built-in one, or the same number and loads earlier.

symptom: ReferenceError: document is not defined or TimepickerUI requires browser environment in Next.js, Nuxt or SvelteKit

fix.text: Create the picker in a hook that runs only in the browser: `useEffect` in React, `onMounted` in Vue and Nuxt, `onMount` in Svelte and SvelteKit. In the Next.js App Router, the file also needs `'use client'`.
Read `document` and `window` only inside that hook as well.
[Server Rendering](https://timepicker-ui.vercel.app/docs/guides/server-rendering) shows the setup for Next.js, Nuxt and SvelteKit.

why: Importing `timepicker-ui` on the server is safe, because no module reads `window` or `document` when it loads. The constructor needs a browser: it throws `TimepickerUI requires browser environment` when `window` is undefined. `ReferenceError: document is not defined` comes from your own code, for example a `document.querySelector()` call in the component body.

symptom: Two pickers open, or events fire twice, in React development mode

fix.text: Return `() => picker.destroy()` from the effect that creates the picker.

why: In development, Strict Mode runs each effect, then its cleanup, then the effect again. Without a cleanup, the first picker stays on the input next to the second one, and both open on click. `destroy()` removes the picker's listeners and its modal.

symptom: Failed to execute 'removeChild' on 'Node' when a React component unmounts

fix.text: Wrap the input in an element with the `tp-ui` class. The picker then uses that element as its root and leaves the input where React rendered it.

why: Given a bare `<input>`, the constructor moves it into a new `div.tp-ui`, and `destroy()` does not remove that div. React still expects the input in its original parent, so removing it can fail. `timepicker-ui-react` renders the wrapper for you.

symptom: The input value does not update React state

fix.text: Set state in `callbacks.onConfirm`. It runs when the user confirms a time, after the picker has written it to the input.
With `timepicker-ui-react`, pass `value` and update it in `onConfirm`.

why: The picker sets `input.value` directly and does not dispatch `input` or `change` events, so React's `onChange` never runs.

symptom: Listeners or a modal stay after a route change

fix.text: Call `picker.destroy()` in your framework's cleanup hook: the function returned from `useEffect` in React, `onBeforeUnmount` in Vue, `ngOnDestroy` in Angular, or the function returned from `onMount` in Svelte.

why: An open modal sits in `<body>`, or in the `ui.appendTo` element, outside your component. If the route changes while the picker is open, the modal stays, and by default the page scroll stays locked. `destroy()` removes the modal, the picker's listeners and the scroll lock.

symptom: ui.mode: 'wheel' or 'compact-wheel' still shows a clock

fix.text: Import `WheelPlugin` from `timepicker-ui/plugins/wheel` and register it once, before creating the picker.

why: Without the plugin, the picker falls back to the clock face and emits `error` with the message `WheelPlugin is not registered. Import and register it: PluginRegistry.register(WheelPlugin)`.
